arxiv-2006-14510.title: Quantum Computing for Finance: State of the Art and Future Prospects
arxiv-2006-14510.creator: DANIEL J. EGGER 1 , CLAUDIO GAMBELLA 1 , JAKUB MARECEK 1 , SCOTT MCFADDIN 1 , MARTIN MEVISSEN 1 , RUDY RAYMOND 1, ANDREA SIMONETTO 1, STEFAN WOERNER 1 , ELENA YNDURAIN 1
arxiv-2006-14510.description: Abstract This paper outlines our point of view regarding the applicability, state of the art, and potential of quantum computing for problems in finance. We provide an introduction to quantum computing as well as a survey on problem classes in finance that are computationally challenging classically and for which quantum computing algorithms are promising.

arxiv-2112-03471.title: Voxelized 3D Feature Aggregation for Multiview Detection PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2112-03471.creator: Jiahao Ma, Jinguang Tong, Shan Wang, Zicheng Duan, Chuong Nguyen
arxiv-2112-03471.description: Abstract Multi-view detection incorporates multiple camera views to alleviate occlusion in crowded scenes, where the state-of-the-art approaches adopt homography transformations to project multi-view features to the ground plane. However, we find that simple 2D transformations do not take into account the object’s height, leading to ground plane features.

arxiv-2203-10184.title: Study of Electroweak Phase Transition in Exotic Higgs Decays at the CEPC
arxiv-2203-10184.creator: Zhen Wang, Xuliang Zhu, Elham E Khoda, Shih-Chieh Hsu, Nikolaos Konstantinidis, Ke Li, Shu Li, Michael J. Ramsey-Musolf, Yanda Wu, Yuwen E. Zhang
arxiv-2203-10184.description: Abstract A strong first-order electroweak phase transition (EWPT) can be induced by light new physics weakly coupled to the Higgs. This study focuses on a scenario in which the first-order EWPT is driven by a light scalar s s with a mass between 15-60 GeV.

arxiv-2406-15917.title: To Err is Robotic: Rapid Value-Based Trial-and-Error during Deployment
arxiv-2406-15917.creator: Maximilian Du, Alexander Khazatsky, Tobias Gerstenberg, Chelsea Finn
arxiv-2406-15917.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Maximilian Du, Alexander Khazatsky, Tobias Gerstenberg, Chelsea Finn. When faced with a novel scenario, it can be hard to succeed on the first attempt. In these challenging situations, it is important to know how to retry quickly and meaningfully. Retrying behavior can emerge naturally in robots trained on diverse data, but such robot policies will typically only exhibit undirected retrying behavior and may not terminate a suboptimal approach before an unrecoverable mistake.

arxiv-2501-05132.title: CorrDiff: Adaptive Delay-aware Detector with Temporal Cue Inputs for Real-time Object Detection
arxiv-2501-05132.creator: Xiang Zhang, Chenchen Fu, Yufei Cui, Lan Yi, Yuyang Sun, Weiwei Wu, Xue Liu
arxiv-2501-05132.description: Abstract Real-time object detection takes an essential part in the decision-making process of numerous real-world applications, including collision avoidance and path planning in autonomous driving systems. This paper presents a novel real-time streaming perception method named CorrDiff, designed to tackle the challenge of delays in real-time detection systems.

arxiv-2508-10988.title: Observable Optimization for Precision Theory: Machine Learning Energy Correlators
arxiv-2508-10988.creator: Arindam Bhattacharya, Katherine Fraser, and Matthew D. Schwartz
arxiv-2508-10988.description: Abstract The practice of collider physics typically involves the marginalization of multi-dimensional collider data to uni-dimensional observables relevant for some physics task. In many cases, such as classification or anomaly detection, the observable can be arbitrarily complicated, such as the output of a neural network.

pmc-10670206.title: STAT2 Controls Colorectal Tumorigenesis and Resistance to Anti-Cancer Drugs
pmc-10670206.creator: Mircea T. Chiriac, Zsuzsanna Hracsko, Christoph Becker, Markus F. Neurath
pmc-10670206.description: Simple SummaryDespite recent improvements in survival rates, colorectal cancer is still responsible for millions of premature deaths worldwide. A better understanding of the steps that lead from chronic inflammation to cancer progression could offer new therapeutic options and save many lives.

pmc-10707856.title: Exploring the Differential Impact of Salt Stress on Root Colonization Adaptation Mechanisms in Plant Growth-Promoting Rhizobacteria
pmc-10707856.creator: Lorena del Rosario Cappellari, Pablo Cesar Bogino, Fiorela Nievas, Walter Giordano, Erika Banchio
pmc-10707856.description: Salinity inhibits plant growth by affecting physiological processes, but soil microorganisms like plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) can alleviate abiotic stress and enhance crop productivity. However, it should be noted that rhizobacteria employ different approaches to deal with salt stress conditions and successfully colonize roots.

pmc-12502370.title: Mesenchymal stromal cells attenuate primary sjogren’s syndrome by modulating PD-1+CXCR5− T peripheral helper cells via galectin-1
pmc-12502370.creator: Shiyi Zhang, Fanzhang Yin, Rui Chai, Tao Li, Yingying Gao, Xiaoxiang Chen, Genhong Yao, Xiaojun Tang, Xiaojuan Han, Betty P Tsao, Linyu Geng, Lingyun Sun
pmc-12502370.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo investigate the role of PD-1+CXCR5-CD4+ peripheral helper T (Tph) cells in patients with primary Sjogren’s syndrome (pSS) and to assess the therapeutic efficacy of mesenchymal stromal cells (MSC) in pSS patients through modulating Tph cells.MethodsWe measured the frequencies and numbers of T cell subsets, including Tph cells, follicular helper T (Tfh) cells, and Treg cells, as well as the levels of IL-21 in patients with pSS and healthy controls (HC).

pmc-12578920.title: Spectral efficiency enhancement in multiuser NOMA over Nakagami-m fading channels through power allocation and pairing strategies under hardware and SIC imperfections
pmc-12578920.creator: R Dipinkrishnan, Vinoth Babu Kumaravelu
pmc-12578920.description: Non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) is a key enabler for future sixth-generation (6G) and massive machine-type communication networks, offering superior sum spectral efficiency (SSE) and user fairness compared to traditional orthogonal multiple access (OMA) schemes. However, practical deployments face challenges due to hardware impairments (HI) and imperfect successive interference cancellation (iSIC), which cause signal distortion and residual interference, degrading system reliability.

pmc-12584457.title: CT radiomics-based explainable machine learning model for accurate differentiation of malignant and benign endometrial tumors: a two-center study
pmc-12584457.creator: Tingrui Zhang, Honglin Wu, Zekun Jiang, Yingying Wang, Rui Ye, Huiming Ni, Chang Liu, Jin Cao, Xuan Sun, Rong Shao, Xiaorong Wei, Yingchun Sun
pmc-12584457.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectivesThis study aimed to develop and validate a CT radiomics-based explainable machine learning model for precise diagnosing of malignancy and benignity specifically in endometrial cancer (EC) patients.MethodsA total of 83 EC patients from two centers, including 46 with malignant and 37 with benign conditions, were included, with data split into a training set (n = 59) and a testing set (n = 24).

pmc-12834996.title: Steerable terahertz beams using surface waves on an active metasurface
pmc-12834996.creator: Yaseman Shiri, Jeffrey Lei, Yasith Amarasinghe, Hou-Tong Chen, Chun-Chieh Chang, Michael P Lilly, Sadhvikas Addamane, Daniel M Mittleman
pmc-12834996.description: The development of dynamic components for controlling wave fronts in the sub-terahertz region of the electromagnetic spectrum has emerged as a frontier research topic for many applications in sensing and communications. One approach which has attracted much attention involves the use of active metasurfaces, tiled arrays of sub-wavelength elements with properties that can be reconfigured via external actuation.

pmc-12990364.title: Ultrasound-modified soy protein-hyaluronic acid conjugates for swallowing-friendly high internal phase pickering emulsion gels: structure, properties, and applications
pmc-12990364.creator: Yang Wang, Zhanqiang Ma, Yueru Liu, Yuetong Gong
pmc-12990364.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). With the increasing global aging population, there is a growing demand for safe and nutritious specialized foods tailored to individuals with dysphagia. However, designing foods with suitable texture, stability, and swallowability remains a significant challenge. This study explores the use of high-intensity ultrasound (HIU)-modified soy protein isolate (SPI)/hyaluronic acid (HA) complexes and conjugates to fabricate high internal phase Pickering emulsion gels (HIPPEGs) suitable for dysphagia patients. The formation of the SPI/HA conjugate was demonstrated by SDS-PAGE and degree of grafting.

pmc-13112341.title: Analysis of low-benefit subgroups in breast-conserving surgery: Implications for clinical decision-making (Review)
pmc-13112341.creator: Weicheng Lin, Lan Luo, Guiping Guo, Huan Lin
pmc-13112341.description: Breast-conserving surgery (BCS) with radiotherapy is a standard treatment for early-stage breast cancer, offering survival outcomes equivalent to mastectomy while preserving breast appearance and improving quality of life. However, BCS suitability and effectiveness vary notably among patients due to differences in age, comorbidities, tumor biology, breast anatomy and psychosocial factors.

pmc-13263735.title: Quantum federated learning for autonomous vehicle cybersecurity: An analytical review of architectures and threat landscapes
pmc-13263735.creator: Sowmya T, Raghavendra M Devadas
pmc-13263735.description: Highlights•Quantum Federated Learning — integrating CRYSTALS-Dilithium gradient authentication, QKD-secured aggregation, and quantum Byzantine filtering — is proposed as a reference architecture with a structured 2025–2030 roadmap addressing seven evidence-grounded research gaps toward standardised automotive deployment.•A multi-dimensional risk matrix across 46 studies reveals that ML adversarial attacks pose the highest FL-specific vulnerability exposure (0.85) and detection difficulty (0.

pmc-13627933.title: Associations between El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and tuberculosis incidence in China: a nationwide study
pmc-13627933.creator: Xiaopeng Qin, Yizhang Xia, Jiang Xue, Xudong Zhou, Wenjie Tao, Yukang Wu, Hongchang Zhang, Ying Chen, Zhenyu Lin, Lanwei Nong, Kechang He, Zhendong Qin, Tiejun Zhou, Zhouhua Xie, Jie Ma
pmc-13627933.description: BackgroundClimate variability may influence tuberculosis (TB) burden, but associations between the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and TB incidence remain poorly characterized across China.ObjectiveTo quantify associations of ENSO and meteorological factors with TB notification incidence and assess regional and age-specific heterogeneity.
